rule: These checks are deliberately not claimed by local unit tests. Execute them after pushing the repository and attach the terminal run's debug manifest and relevant redacted logs.
prerequisites: A target PC or target container matching the intended deployment
A real webpage MCP client supporting OAuth
HTTPS or an approved loopback development URL
A configured native isolation helper/container with no private-vault mount
A real LaTeX toolchain when RE_CTM_LATEX_POLICY=required
External theorem/web retrieval connectivity if used by the reasoning workflow

checks.name: OAuth discovery and dynamic registration
steps: Run Re-CTM on 127.0.0.1 without RE_CTM_SERVER_URL or RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD; record the generated Re-CTM OAuth authorization key shown only in the local operator terminal, then start a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel after the server is already listening and confirm no Re-CTM restart is needed when the random trycloudflare.com hostname appears.
Fetch OAuth authorization-server and protected-resource metadata through the Quick Tunnel and confirm issuer/resource/endpoint URLs use the public HTTPS trycloudflare.com origin.
Complete the browser authorization form through the Quick Tunnel and confirm its Origin-bearing POST is accepted as an OAuth route while an unapproved external Origin sent to /mcp is still rejected.

After submitting the authorization key, confirm the browser follows the 302 to the registered ChatGPT callback and Re-CTM subsequently receives POST /oauth/token rather than restarting a fresh authorization request.
Run scripts/smoke_oauth_mcp.py against the public base URL and save its redacted report.
Connect the webpage client to /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and the MCP URL.
Confirm DCR creates a client and the browser is redirected to /oauth/authorize.
Complete PKCE authorization and token exchange.
Repeat with an explicit RE_CTM_SERVER_URL and confirm forwarded Host headers cannot replace that fixed OAuth origin.
expected: No static bearer or no-auth path is offered.

When no OAuth password is configured, a high-entropy authorization key is generated for the serve session, displayed to the local operator, accepted on the first OAuth page, and absent from structured logs, reports, HTTP payloads, and persisted state.
Dynamic OAuth origin works only with a loopback-bound server and the tunnel's trusted local proxy request; non-loopback dynamic bind is rejected.
An access token issued for the public tunnel origin is rejected when replayed against a different effective origin.
The client reaches tools/list only with a valid OAuth access token.
Debug events contain fingerprints, not raw codes, secrets, passwords, or tokens.

checks.name: Fixed tool catalog across native modes and workflow states
steps: Confirm scripts/smoke_oauth_mcp.py reports exactly 24 public tools (18 CTM Native + 6 Rethlas façade tools) and a modern non-inheritance result.
Confirm superseded Rethlas protocol names such as rethlas_next/rethlas_status remain callable as hidden compatibility aliases but are absent from tools/list.
Capture tools/list in safe, trusted, and dangerous native modes.
Capture tools/list during generator, branch, join, verifier, and repair states.
expected: Catalog and schemas are identical.
Authorization changes server-side call results rather than catalog visibility.

checks.name: Dangerous native isolation
steps: Install bubblewrap on Linux or provide an independently reviewed external helper.
Run `re-ctm attest-native --backend bubblewrap --workspace <workspace> --data-root <data-root> --private-root <private-root>` without enabling native execution.

Run `python3 scripts/manual_native_isolation_test.py --backend bubblewrap --workspace <workspace> --data-root <data-root> --private-root <private-root> --output native-isolation-validation.json` and review every check.

Run Re-CTM with native_mode=dangerous on Linux with bwrap installed and confirm the built-in Bubblewrap backend is selected automatically and startup attestation succeeds without an acknowledgement flag.
Create arbitrary non-product-named CLI toolchains in a Conda-style prefix, a bin/Executables prefix, and a PATH symlink target; confirm all are discovered without application-name configuration.
Place an additional CLI plus runtime outside PATH, expose it with RE_CTM_NATIVE_EXEC_ALLOW_ROOTS, and confirm it executes by name through the extended sandbox PATH.
Attempt to declare relative, missing, `/`, complete-home, workspace-overlapping, data-overlapping, and private-overlapping allow roots and confirm startup/check-config fails closed.
Attempt to mutate every exposed toolchain root and confirm Bubblewrap presents it read-only; point a PATH symlink into private state and confirm the target is excluded.
Run representative installed tools such as SageMath, Magma, Mathematica/wolframscript, or site-local equivalents when available, while configured Re-CTM data/private roots remain invisible.
Use exec_command to enumerate mounts and attempt direct reads of the configured Re-CTM data/private roots.
Attempt privilege escalation, parent-environment recovery, namespace creation, and access through interpreters or nested shells.
expected: Native workspace remains usable.
Private run store is not mounted or otherwise reachable.
The helper response is nonce-bound and attests mount, user, PID, environment, capability, and network properties.
The effective toolchain view is application-agnostic, canonical, ancestor-collapsed, read-only, diagnostic, and disjoint from workspace/data/private trust domains.
Safe mode has a private network namespace; trusted/dangerous network behavior matches the selected native policy.
Dangerous never grants a rethlas_* capability or finalization authority.

checks.name: Sequential branch-domain information barrier
steps: Create at least three materially different decomposition plans.
Execute branch A, seal it, then enter branch B and branch C.
Try rethlas_read against prior and future branch identifiers before join.
Enter join only after all branches are sealed.
expected: Every branch receives the same snapshot hash.
Cross-branch reads are denied until join.
Sealed capability reuse is denied.
Join receives all branch results simultaneously.

checks.name: Verifier data firewall and mechanical verdict
steps: Reach verifier state with a complete proof.tex.
Attempt to read generation memory, branch results, steering, and join internals.
Submit a report whose model-supplied verdict conflicts with its findings.
expected: All generation-private reads are denied.
Server computes correct only when critical_errors and gaps are both empty.
Wrong findings route to repair and cannot create proof_verified.tex.

checks.name: Browser disconnect, resume, steering, and cancellation
steps: Disconnect the webpage after a task is issued.
Reconnect with the same OAuth client and call rethlas_resume.
Queue steering and confirm it appears only at a safe generator/repair checkpoint.
Cancel another run and attempt further writes with its previous capability.
expected: State survives browser disconnect.
Steering is not exposed to verifier.
Cancelled run is sealed and previous capabilities fail.

checks.name: Real LaTeX gate and verified artifact
steps: Run on Linux with RE_CTM_LATEX_POLICY=required, bubblewrap, and a real latexmk installation.
Submit malformed, external-input, shell-escape, and valid self-contained documents.
Create a host-only readable LaTeX class or file outside the compiler scratch directory and confirm the proof cannot load it even by absolute path.
Complete a correct verification report for the valid document.

Advance the MCP workflow with rethlas_step until done and confirm the returned workspace_export_path exists under the native workspace without a separate export command; repeat the terminal call and confirm the identical file is reported unchanged.
Call rethlas_artifact with action=export to a new workspace-relative .tex path, then retry the same path without expected_sha256 and confirm the overwrite is denied.
expected: Unsafe or uncompilable LaTeX routes to repair, and Re-CTM never falls back to compiling model-generated TeX directly on the host.
The compiler receives only a scratch workspace plus read-only system TeX/toolchain roots; Re-CTM private state is not mounted.
Only a compiled proof with empty findings reaches done.
The sole final delivery artifact is proof_verified.tex.
The MCP completion path automatically writes the verified bytes to rethlas-output/<run_id>/proof_verified.tex or the requested export_path, and identical retries are idempotent.
The controlled export writes exactly the finalized bytes inside the native workspace and refuses baseline-free overwrite.

checks.name: Rethlas methodology behavior acceptance
steps: Submit a concrete mathematical proof request in ordinary natural language without naming rethlas_start and confirm the MCP client follows the server instructions by starting and completing a Rethlas run; separately request a direct informal answer and confirm the explicit opt-out is respected.
Use representative easy, difficult, citation-heavy, counterexample-sensitive, and repair-requiring math problems.

In a fresh webpage/model context with no prior Re-CTM protocol knowledge, inspect each returned task contract and complete at least one easy end-to-end run without any JSON-shape/schema correction; confirm write_contract, commit_action, commit_payload_schema, and a valid submission example/template are present at every model-active state.

Inspect memory channels, multiple plan generation, server-issued plan/subgoal ids, incremental direct screening, one-branch-per-plan work, all-branch join, failure synthesis, replanning, verification audits, and changed-proof repair.

During direct screening intentionally submit only a subset of plan/subgoal results; confirm the server stays in direct_proving, returns exact missing ids, retains accepted progress, and advances only after coverage is complete without requiring plan status or branch_plans to be echoed.

Trigger one recoverable rethlas_step validation error during a later write after an earlier write succeeded; confirm recoverable=true, retryable=true, writes_retained=true, failed_write identifies the rejected record, the fresh capability can continue without replaying the retained record, and the superseded capability is revoked. Separately confirm a stale/foreign capability remains a hard permission failure.

Create two active runs, intentionally pair run A's capability with run B's run_id in rethlas_step, and confirm CAPABILITY_RUN_MISMATCH is returned before either run receives a logical write or a fresh task. Confirm the original capability remains usable with its original run. Also verify façade schemas reject malformed/edited capability strings and operation-specific irrelevant fields rather than silently ignoring them.
Use rethlas_retrieve for nontrivial claims; for useful results, inspect the source paper context/proof and persist definitions, applicability checks, and identifiers before relying on them.
expected: Concrete proof/derivation/repair/verification requests route into Rethlas by default rather than ending as an unverified chat-only proof.
Core Rethlas methodology is observably preserved despite sequential domains.
A fresh model can follow the task-provided zero-guess contracts without reading server source or learning hidden JSON requirements from failures.
Failures remain queryable and influence new plans.
External results include complete statements and applicability checks.
Operator judges the target 95-percent functional-equivalence criterion.

checks.name: Coding Tools MCP 18-tool compatibility
steps: Capture tools/list from the reference Coding Tools MCP and Re-CTM, and compare the 18 CTM native names, order, required fields, enums, defaults, and annotations.
Exercise read_file, list_dir, list_files, search_text, apply_patch, Git tools, request_permissions, and view_image against the same disposable workspace.

With the Re-CTM bubblewrap backend enabled, run a long command that returns command_id, poll with write_stdin, page retained stdout/stderr with read_output, interact with a tty=true command, and terminate another command with kill_command.
Repeat command lifecycle checks in safe, trusted, and dangerous native modes and confirm dangerous does not grant any rethlas_* workflow capability.

Trigger one command timeout and one explicit kill_command and inspect termination.source, requested_timeout_ms, elapsed_ms, observed_signal, term_sent_by_re_ctm, and kill_sent_by_re_ctm. If a real CAS process is later killed externally, confirm Re-CTM reports external_or_unknown unless it has evidence that it sent the terminating signal.
expected: No CTM native tool is missing from Re-CTM; tools/list exposes exactly 18 CTM native tools plus 6 Rethlas façade tools, while superseded Rethlas protocol names remain callable as hidden aliases.
Existing CTM-style calls using patch envelopes and cmd/workdir command arguments remain accepted.
Long-running command IDs remain usable through write_stdin, read_output, and kill_command for the lifetime of the Re-CTM server process.
Any documented Re-CTM differences are security-boundary adaptations rather than missing CTM lifecycle functionality.
Termination provenance is additive diagnostics and does not alter the reference CTM timeout/TERM/KILL lifecycle.

checks.name: v0.2 Verified Research Workspace acceptance
steps: On a disposable copy of a dev6/v0.1 private state directory containing at least one terminal run and one in-progress run, start v0.2.1, confirm the state schema migrates additively, and resume the old in-progress run under workflow protocol 1 without acquiring proof_manifest requirements.

Create a research project and OPEN claims through the public Rethlas façade, then start a project-linked protocol-2 run with workflow_mode=auto or compact. Confirm the run receives a frozen project snapshot hash and Native dangerous cannot read the private registry directly.

Complete a direct local lemma through the compact lane and confirm it still traverses LaTeX validation, independent verifier, and finalizer before one immutable VERIFIED revision is promoted. Repeat terminal delivery and confirm no duplicate revision is created.

Create a CONDITIONAL dependency carrying an explicit condition such as GRH, use its frozen revision in a later proof_manifest, and confirm the downstream promoted revision mechanically inherits the condition rather than relying on a model-supplied status label.

Start two project runs from the same claim base revision, let one promote first, then finish the other. Confirm the second mathematical run remains done/correct while registry promotion records an optimistic-concurrency conflict instead of overwriting the newer active revision.

Force one registry-promotion attempt to fail after a mathematically correct run reaches done. Confirm final_tex remains available, the run stays done/correct, promotion remains retryable/pending, and a later terminal rethlas_step retries promotion without re-running the proof.

After a VERIFIED claim revision exists, create a newer OPEN revision and start another project-linked run. Confirm the frozen snapshot still contains the historical VERIFIED revision as an eligible dependency while exposing its superseded lifecycle status.

Run a reference-using proof. Omit the material reference audit once and confirm the server mechanically inserts a verification gap; then audit the same reference as SOURCE_VERIFIED or INDEPENDENTLY_REDERIVED with assumptions/notation/source checks plus evidence_basis/evidence_locator and confirm a correct proof can finalize. Confirm a LeanSearch/OpenAlex discovery snapshot alone is rejected as SOURCE_VERIFIED original-source evidence.

Use rethlas_retrieve theorem_search plus paper_search/paper_lookup/theorem_context on real network connectivity, including an author/title/keywords-only paper search. Confirm results have stable reference ids/source provenance, paper operations use the configured fixed provider, redirects cannot leave the allowed HTTPS provider host, and no public argument permits an arbitrary URL fetch.

Inspect the verifier task for a project-linked proof and confirm it sees only the dependency revisions declared in proof_manifest, not unrelated project claims, speculative notes, generation memory, branches, steering, or generator confidence.

Retrieve proof_manifest, reference_audit, project_manifest, and project_summary_tex through rethlas_artifact; export the project manifest/summary to workspace and confirm they contain claim/revision/status/hash/dependency/condition/audit facts but no private reasoning, owner/OAuth material, or capability handles. Put an unsafe external-file command such as \input in an OPEN claim and confirm project_summary_tex is refused while project_manifest remains available.

Force one compact proof to fail verification twice and confirm the first wrong verdict enters repair while the second changes the effective mode to full and continues at explore. Separately exercise compact assembler outcome=escalate.
expected: Schema migration preserves old workflow state and protocol compatibility while refusing a database from a newer unsupported runtime.
Project state remains private from Native dangerous and owner isolation applies to all project/claim/artifact reads and mutations.
VERIFIED/CONDITIONAL revisions originate only from mechanically finalized correct runs, are immutable, idempotent by source run, and never overwrite a concurrent newer revision.
Registry promotion is a non-fatal second phase after mathematical finalization: promotion errors cannot invalidate verified LaTeX and are retried idempotently on later terminal calls.
Compact mode reduces exploration only; it never bypasses LaTeX, independent verification, repair, or finalization.

Frozen project snapshots make dependency resolution reproducible, retain historical VERIFIED/CONDITIONAL revisions even after later OPEN revisions supersede them, and propagate conditional hypotheses mechanically through declared dependencies.
Material references cannot silently pass without a resolved verifier audit and source/provenance evidence remains traceable.
Paper-aware retrieval is useful on the target network but remains bounded and fixed-provider rather than an arbitrary URL fetcher.
Portable project artifacts are sufficient for research/project management without exposing private chain-of-thought-like workflow memory.

checks.name: Minimal terminal observer acceptance
steps: On a target machine, open a terminal in a disposable project directory and run re-ctm tui with RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD unset. Confirm the displayed workspace is the current directory, the local/fixed MCP URL is correct, and the generated authorization key appears only after a successful bind.

Connect the real webpage MCP client, complete DCR/PKCE OAuth, and confirm the terminal status advances from waiting for authorization to authorization accepted/token issued/connected without repeating connected for every authenticated MCP request.

Issue several native and Rethlas tool calls and confirm the terminal shows only tool name/start/success-or-safe-error facts, never arguments, results, problem/proof contents, access tokens, authorization codes, capabilities, or client secrets.
Start the same setup with an explicit RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD and confirm the TUI prints configured externally rather than echoing the password.

Run plain re-ctm tui through an independently managed Cloudflare Quick Tunnel without RE_CTM_SERVER_URL. Confirm the TUI does not claim to own that external process and only updates the public origin after the trusted loopback proxy request resolves it.
Stress tool calls while slowing or breaking the terminal consumer and confirm MCP/tool execution remains responsive; verify no idle polling behavior is observable when no events occur.
Scan debug JSONL, SQLite state, validation reports, and project ledgers for the generated authorization key and confirm it is absent.
expected: The TUI is optional presentation only and re-ctm serve remains behaviorally compatible for headless use.
Terminal rendering failure, queue pressure, or a closed output pipe cannot change tool success/failure or OAuth authorization semantics.
The generated OAuth key remains local-terminal-only secret material and explicitly configured passwords are never echoed by the TUI.
Plain tui adds no database/log polling, extra model/network request, token-usage estimation, public-tool change, workflow-state change, persistence-schema change, or tunnel process.

checks.name: One-command Quick Tunnel TUI acceptance
steps: On a target machine with cloudflared installed, open a disposable project directory and run re-ctm tui --quick-tunnel --native-mode dangerous with RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD and RE_CTM_PORT unset. Confirm Re-CTM chooses an available loopback port without fuser/pkill and displays both the generated authorization key and a real HTTPS *.trycloudflare.com/mcp URL.

Connect the real webpage MCP client to the displayed public MCP URL, complete DCR/PKCE OAuth, and exercise both a Native tool and a Rethlas workflow call while the same terminal reports authentication and tool-call state.

Repeat with an explicit --port and with RE_CTM_PORT to confirm each value is respected; repeat with a stale RE_CTM_SERVER_URL and confirm --quick-tunnel uses the dynamically resolved TryCloudflare origin for that session without rewriting the environment or persisted configuration.

Temporarily hide cloudflared from PATH and confirm --quick-tunnel reports that it is unavailable while the local MCP server remains running. Separately force cloudflared to exit early and confirm the same local-service degradation.

Set RE_CTM OAuth/token/capability secrets and Cloudflare named-tunnel credential environment variables, launch --quick-tunnel under process/environment inspection, and confirm the child receives none of those credential variables.

Press Ctrl-C after the Quick Tunnel is connected, confirm Re-CTM exits cleanly and the cloudflared child created by that TUI session is gone; confirm unrelated pre-existing cloudflared processes are untouched.
expected: The common remote-client path is one command: re-ctm tui --quick-tunnel --native-mode dangerous.
Quick Tunnel mode is explicit opt-in; plain tui and serve create no cloudflared process and retain their previous performance profile.
Only strict HTTPS *.trycloudflare.com output becomes the public MCP URL; Quick Tunnel cannot inherit Re-CTM secrets or named-tunnel credentials.
Tunnel failure never kills the local MCP service, and shutdown only terminates the child process owned by this TUI session.
Real webpage/browser compatibility remains a manual target assertion even though deterministic lifecycle tests and a real local-network Quick Tunnel smoke pass.
evidence: Local source smoke on 2026-08-31 used the installed cloudflared with isolated /tmp Re-CTM data roots: --quick-tunnel selected an OS-assigned loopback port and produced a real HTTPS *.trycloudflare.com/mcp URL.
A real HTTPS request through that Quick Tunnel to /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returned resource and authorization_servers bound to the same random TryCloudflare origin.

A separate timeout/SIGINT source smoke exited Re-CTM with status 130 and left no matching cloudflared process; deterministic tests cover owned TERM-to-KILL escalation. Real webpage DCR/PKCE and target dangerous-mode tool calls remain pending.
